subject: Literacy
title: Action rhymes
objectives: Children will join in actions and words of a short rhyme.
Children will fill in a missing word with support.
content: Finger rhymes, action songs and a rhyme with a small story, with children filling in missing words.
teachingActivities: Say or sing each rhyme slowly with big actions; repeat it several times; pause before the last word of a line so children can fill it in; use the same rhymes all week.
learnerActivities: Join in the actions and words of short rhymes and fill in a missing word with support.
resources: A basket of toy fish, a toy spider and a toy bus
assessment: Observe whether each child joins in at least two rhymes with actions and says the last word when you pause.
expectedOutcomes: Joins in at least two rhymes with actions.
Says the last word of a line when the teacher pauses.

lessons.title: Two little hands
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will copy the finger actions of a short rhyme.
successCriteria: Copies at least one finger action
Joins in with a word or sound
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, copy sounds and beats, greet others and respond to their names.
lessons.starter: Hold up both hands and wiggle your fingers. Say "Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. Can you wiggle too?"
teacherActivities: Say the rhyme "Ten little fingers, wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. Hide them in your lap, giggle, giggle, giggle." Show the actions slowly.
Say the rhyme again and do the actions with the puppet.
Say the rhyme again and pause before the last word of each line.
Let one child lead with the puppet while the others do the actions.
learnerActivities: Children watch and wiggle their fingers.
Children copy the wiggle and the hiding action.
Children say "wiggle" or "giggle" or make the sound.
Child leads and friends copy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say the rhyme "Ten little fingers, wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. Hide them in your lap, giggle, giggle, giggle." Show the actions slowly. Children: Children watch and wiggle their fingers.
Step 2. Teacher: Say the rhyme again and do the actions with the puppet. Children: Children copy the wiggle and the hiding action.
Step 3. Teacher: Say the rhyme again and pause before the last word of each line. Children: Children say "wiggle" or "giggle" or make the sound.
Step 4. Teacher: Let one child lead with the puppet while the others do the actions. Children: Child leads and friends copy.

practical.title: Fingers play
steps: Sit in a circle with space to move hands.
Say the rhyme and do the actions together.
Repeat three times, faster each time.
practical.safety: Keep hands away from faces and eyes. Stop the game if any child becomes upset or tired.

differentiation.support: Move the child’s fingers gently for the actions and say the words with them.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach the rhyme actions to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at the end?

expectedOutcomes: Joins in with words or sounds
lessons.conclusion: Sing the rhyme once more very quietly and hide the hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing "Ten little fingers" at bath time and do the actions with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "copy the finger actions of a short rhyme" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Ten little fingers, wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. Hide them in your lap, giggle, giggle, giggle.

lessons.title: Five little fish
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will join in the actions of a counting rhyme with fish.
successCriteria: Says a word or the number in the rhyme
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, copy sounds and beats, greet others and respond to their names.
resources: Five toy fish or paper fish
A blue cloth for the water
lessons.starter: Spread the blue cloth and put five fish on it. Say "Splash! The fish are swimming."
teacherActivities: Say the rhyme "Five little fish swimming in the sea. Splash, splash, splash, come to me." Show the swimming action with a hand.
Say the rhyme again and move one fish at a time to you on the word "me".
Let each child pick a fish and swim it across the cloth.
learnerActivities: Children watch and copy the hand swimming.
Children say "splash" and watch the fish.
Children say "splash" or clap.
Child swims the fish and says "splash".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say the rhyme "Five little fish swimming in the sea. Splash, splash, splash, come to me." Show the swimming action with a hand. Children: Children watch and copy the hand swimming.
Step 2. Teacher: Say the rhyme again and move one fish at a time to you on the word "me". Children: Children say "splash" and watch the fish.
Step 3. Teacher: Pause before "splash" and wait. Children: Children say "splash" or clap.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick a fish and swim it across the cloth. Children: Child swims the fish and says "splash".

practical.title: Fish in the sea
steps: Spread a blue cloth on the floor.
Each child holds a paper fish and swims it across the cloth.
practical.safety: Use soft paper or cloth fish with no small parts. Keep the cloth flat so no one trips.

differentiation.support: Hold the fish together and swim it with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count the fish as they swim to the teacher.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the fish to sleep under the cloth and whisper goodnight.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing the fish rhyme at bath time and swim a toy in the water.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "join in the actions of a counting rhyme with fish" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Five little fish swimming in the sea. Splash, splash, splash, come to me.

lessons.title: Spider and bus
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will join in the actions of two action songs.
successCriteria: Does at least two actions in a song
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, copy sounds and beats, greet others and respond to their names.
resources: A toy bus or a bus picture
lessons.starter: Walk your fingers like a spider up your arm and say "The spider is climbing up."
teacherActivities: Sing "The little spider climbs up, up, up. Down comes the rain, splash, splash. The spider climbs up again." Show climbing and rain actions.
Sing the song again and wait for the children to do the actions without help.
Sing "The wheels on the bus go round and round" with the wheel action.
Let each child choose spider or bus and lead the song.
learnerActivities: Children copy the climbing and the falling rain.
Children do the actions on their own.
Children make circles with their arms.
Child chooses and sings with the group.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing "The little spider climbs up, up, up. Down comes the rain, splash, splash. The spider climbs up again." Show climbing and rain actions. Children: Children copy the climbing and the falling rain.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the song again and wait for the children to do the actions without help. Children: Children do the actions on their own.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing "The wheels on the bus go round and round" with the wheel action. Children: Children make circles with their arms.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose spider or bus and lead the song. Children: Child chooses and sings with the group.

practical.title: Song choice
steps: Show the spider and bus pictures.
A child picks one and the group sings it.
Repeat so each child has a turn.
practical.safety: Leave enough space for arm movements and keep children from bumping. Keep voices gentle.

differentiation.support: Do the actions with the child and sing in their ear.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make up a new action for a line of the song.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Does the correct action at the right time
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the spider and the bus.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing "The wheels on the bus" at home and do the actions with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "join in the actions of two action songs" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: The wheels on the bus go round and round, round and round, round and round.

lessons.title: A rhyme with a story
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will say the last word of a line in a story rhyme when the teacher pauses.
successCriteria: Fills in a missing word with support
Does the actions of the rhyme
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, copy sounds and beats, greet others and respond to their names.
resources: Picture cards of a hen, an egg and a chick
lessons.starter: Show the hen puppet and say "Cluck, cluck. The hen has something in the basket."
teacherActivities: Say the rhyme "Little hen, little hen, what do you lay? An egg, an egg, every day." Show the picture cards.
Say it again and pause before "egg".
Say "Little hen, little hen, what comes out? A chick, a chick, cheep, cheep, shout!" and show the chick.
Let a child hold the hen puppet and lead the lines.
learnerActivities: Children look and point to the egg.
Children say "egg".
Children say "chick" and "cheep".
Child leads and friends fill in the words.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say the rhyme "Little hen, little hen, what do you lay? An egg, an egg, every day." Show the picture cards. Children: Children look and point to the egg.
Step 2. Teacher: Say it again and pause before "egg". Children: Children say "egg".
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Little hen, little hen, what comes out? A chick, a chick, cheep, cheep, shout!" and show the chick. Children: Children say "chick" and "cheep".
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child hold the hen puppet and lead the lines. Children: Child leads and friends fill in the words.

practical.title: Hen and chick
steps: Hide an egg picture in the basket.
Say the rhyme and ask the children what the hen lays.
Show the egg, then the chick.
practical.safety: Keep pictures flat and clean and supervise sharing. Do not use real eggs.

differentiation.support: Point to the egg picture before you say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say the whole line "An egg, an egg" alone.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What comes out of the egg?

expectedOutcomes: Fills in the last word with support
Does the hen and chick actions
lessons.conclusion: Put the hen to sleep and whisper "Night, night, hen."
lessons.homeConnection: Say the hen rhyme at home and pause for your child to say "egg".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say the last word of a line in a story rhyme when the teacher pauses" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Little hen, little hen, what do you lay? An egg, an egg, every day.

lessons.title: Week 6 rhyme check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child joins in rhymes and fills in missing words.
successCriteria: Joins in actions of a rhyme
Says a word at the pause
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, copy sounds and beats, greet others and respond to their names.
lessons.starter: Sing the finger rhyme and show three rhyme stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: finger rhymes, action songs and a rhyme with a story.
At each station say a rhyme and pause for the last word.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child does the actions and says the word.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: finger rhymes, action songs and a rhyme with a story. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station say a rhyme and pause for the last word. Children: Child does the actions and says the word.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Rhyme stations
practical.safety: Use soft toys and pictures. Supervise each station and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and repeat the rhyme twice.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to lead a rhyme.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: joins in at least two rhymes with actions; fills in a missing word; sings or hums along.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
lessons.conclusion: Sing the goodbye song and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing two rhymes at home and pause for your child to fill in a word.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child joins in rhymes and fills in missing words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
